WM Phoenix Open 2027: parking and getting there

A Phoenix Open ride from Scottsdale Sprinters starts with the day your group is having: the 16th hole with the crew, a client day in hospitality, a round with the golf fans or a Birds Nest night. This guide uses only what the tournament and TPC Scottsdale publish, labels last year’s parking plan as last year’s, and says plainly what is announced closer to the date.

Last updated: September 24, 2026

Where do you park for the WM Phoenix Open 2027, and is it free?

The 2027 parking plan and any parking price are announced closer to the date. In 2026, general parking used remote WestWorld Lots A, B and C, plus a Salt River Fields lot with a free shuttle; ADA parking is Lot 2, at Hayden and Bell. With a chauffeured ride, nobody in the group drives or parks. Last year’s plan, labelled as last year’s: in 2026 the remote general-parking lots were WestWorld Lots A, B and C, open Monday through Sunday and reached from the WestWorld area near Frank Lloyd Wright Boulevard, Thompson Peak Parkway, Pima Road and Bell Road. The 2026 Salt River Fields lot ran Wednesday through Sunday from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., about 7.6 miles south of TPC Scottsdale, with a free shuttle to the tournament. The tournament’s parking answers still link that 2026 map. Also from 2026: general-parking guests were told not to leave Loop 101 at Hayden Road or Scottsdale Road, which were kept for ADA access and credentialed passes because of restrictions on 78th Street and Mayo Boulevard, and to use the Princess Boulevard or Bell Road exits instead. Treat that as last year’s routing until the tournament publishes the 2027 version. Confirmed now: some areas and parking lots are reserved for specific pass types, including event staff, vendors, volunteers, media, charter buses and internal operations, and guests may enter only the areas their pass allows. The ADA lot is Lot 2, at the corner of Hayden and Bell Roads, with a valid handicap placard displayed. The tournament also says parking operations, routes and lot availability may change as the event approaches. The chauffeured alternative: we pick the group up at the hotel or home and unload where traffic staff direct. Nobody hunts for a lot, waits for a remote-lot shuttle or drives home after the 16th hole. Whether a booked Sprinter or coach needs a pass for any lot is not published, so the reservations team confirms the current instruction before the day rather than promising a lot.

Where do rideshares and drop-offs go at the Phoenix Open?

In 2026, rideshare vehicles, taxis and all passenger drop-off and pick-up used Lot R, entered from Pima Road, instead of the public lots; the 2027 plan is announced closer to the date. At the Birds Nest, rideshares use Hartford Drive, south of Princess. A chauffeured vehicle unloads where traffic staff direct. No official page gives a limo, a party bus or a charter a gate or drop-off privilege. The only published line about charters is that some lots are reserved for pass types, charter buses among them, and the tournament has not published how an operator gets that pass. So this page promises no gate, lot or curb: the chauffeur follows traffic staff, and the reservations team passes on any 2027 instruction the tournament publishes. The entrances are the Main Entrance at Bell, the Hayden Entrance and the Fairmont Scottsdale Princess Golf Entrance. Checkpoints stand throughout the area and must be passed before entering designated zones, and some roads and private areas are closed to event guest traffic. Plan the pickup as a place the group can walk to from the entrance it used, not a pin dropped beside a checkpoint. For the ride home, name one meeting point and one transportation lead before the group goes in. The curb you arrived at may not be where a vehicle can wait at the end of play. The lead counts heads, confirms the vehicle’s position with the chauffeur and walks the group there together, rather than everyone chasing a map pin at once.

When is the WM Phoenix Open 2027?

The WM Phoenix Open runs Monday, February 8 to Sunday, February 14, 2027, at TPC Scottsdale. Monday and Tuesday are Ford Free Days with free general admission, and the 4 rounds run Thursday, February 11 to Sunday, February 14: play begins at 7:30 a.m. Thursday and Friday and 9:00 a.m. on the weekend. The week opens early. The Concert in the Coliseum is on Saturday, February 6, 2027, on the 16th hole: Imagine Dragons, with Counting Crows opening, for guests 21 and over, with venue gates at 3:30 p.m. The Carlisle Pro-Am starts at 8:30 a.m. on Monday, February 8, and the Annexus Pro-Am at 8:30 a.m. on Wednesday, February 10, the day the WHOOP Shot at Glory is on the 16th hole at 3:30 p.m. Saturday, February 13 is Green Out Saturday: guests wear green, and a donation goes to the tournament’s Working for Tomorrow fund. The Coors Light Birds Nest runs the evenings of Wednesday, February 10 to Saturday, February 13. The tournament says its agenda is subject to change, so recheck the official schedule in the week before you ride. For a ride, pick the day first, then the arrival. The tournament suggests lining up early for a seat at the 16th hole, especially on Friday and Saturday, when early arrivals are asked to use the Main Entrance. On the Ford Free Days, Monday and Tuesday, no ticket is needed at all.

Where is the Phoenix Open played, and when do the gates open?

The Phoenix Open is played on the Stadium Course at TPC Scottsdale, 17020 North Hayden Road, Scottsdale, AZ 85255. Entry opens each day at 7:00 a.m. at the Main and Princess entrances and at 7:15 a.m. at Hayden; on Friday and Saturday, Hayden opens only once the Main line is in. The three entrances are the Main Entrance at Bell, the Hayden Entrance and the Fairmont Scottsdale Princess Golf Entrance. Guests arriving early on Friday and Saturday are asked to use the Main Entrance; a line may form at Hayden, but Hayden admits guests only after everyone at the Main Entrance is in. Tournament Guest Services is north of Bell Road between Hayden and 82nd Street and opens daily at 7 a.m. The entry times are the tournament’s own answers, written after the 2026 event and not dated for 2027, so recheck them in January. The street address is the host club’s, from TPC Scottsdale’s own site. On the day the tournament routes guests by entrance, lot and signage rather than by street number, and the chauffeur follows its signs and staff. Tournament traffic is not normal traffic. Build the buffer before the time the group wants to be through the gate, count screening and the walk from the unload point, and plan the return as a window rather than a fixed minute: the round, the crowd at the 16th hole and the exits decide it.

Which vehicle fits a Phoenix Open group?

Match the vehicle to the day: hospitality hosts and VIP guests ride the Maybach Jet Sprinter or our other ultra-luxury rides, 16th-hole crews take a Limo Party Sprinter or the Party Bus (28 Pax) for up to 28, and couples and golf fans take an Executive Sprinter or, for a club of up to 29, the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). Corporate hospitality and VIP: the Maybach Jet Sprinter leads, 9 seats with Maybach massage recliners and a wet bar. The Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter seats 15 in a fiber-optic lounge for a Birds Nest night, the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter seats 8 in custom Maybach seats, and the Luxury SUV (Suburban) carries a couple or a small client party of up to 6. A larger hospitality list moves in the executive coaches below. 16th-hole crews: the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) and the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) are limo lounges on wheels for 13 and 16, and the Party Bus (28 Pax) puts 28 on limo seating when the whole crew comes. These are party rides for a group out to celebrate; we never send one as a corporate client vehicle. Couples and golf fans: the Executive Black Sprinter and the Executive White Sprinter seat 14 each in reclining leather, and the Mini Bus (24 Pax) (24 seats) and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) (29 seats) carry a golf club, a supporters’ group or a company outing in one vehicle. Count riders for each direction. A morning arrival for the 16th hole and an evening return after the Birds Nest are often different lists. Anyone leaving with another group comes off the return manifest before seats are assigned; “we will decide at the course” is not a count the chauffeur can plan around when the tournament is releasing traffic.

What is the Coors Light Birds Nest, and how do you get there and back?

The Coors Light Birds Nest is the tournament’s 21-and-over concert tent at 82nd Street and Bell Road, across from the main entrance, from Wednesday, February 10 to Saturday, February 13, 2027. Headliners usually go on at about 8:30 p.m.; rideshares use Hartford Drive, south of Princess, and a booked ride waits for the group. The 2027 lineup so far: Riley Green with Ashley Cooke on Wednesday, Jason Aldean with Josh Ross on Thursday, and Snoop Dogg with T-Pain on Friday. Saturday’s act is to be announced. Valid government-issued ID is required at the gate, and Will Call is at the Birds Nest front gate on 82nd Street and Bell Road, opening at noon Wednesday through Saturday. The gate time is announced closer to the date: the organizer’s own pages do not yet agree on it. Birds Nest parking hours are also listed as to be determined. After the concert, the organizer’s shuttles take guests to the WestWorld of Scottsdale parking used for the tournament. A chauffeured group skips the lot and the shuttle: book the vehicle by the hour for the evening, or a drop-off and a set pickup, and agree the meeting point before the headliner starts. The Birds Nest and the Concert in the Coliseum are both 21 and over, so a group with anyone younger plans the tournament day instead of the concert night.

What can you bring into the Phoenix Open, and what should the day plan include?

The gate allows no opaque bag larger than 6 by 6 by 6 inches and no clear bag larger than 12 by 6 by 12 inches, and admission is a digital AXS ticket. Write the day plan in 5 lines: ready time, entrance, meeting point, one transportation lead and the ride home. General admission for the tournament and for the Birds Nest is a digital AXS Mobile ID ticket; guests without a smartphone can visit Guest Services. Guests 15 and younger get in free, and on the Ford Free Days, Monday, February 8 and Tuesday, February 9, no ticket is needed. Suites and hospitality packages are sold by the tournament, not by us: a ride includes no ticket, pass or parking. Anything bigger than those bag limits, a cooler included, stays on the vehicle. The ready time is when guests are at the pickup point with tickets on their phones, not when they start getting dressed. On Green Out Saturday the tournament asks guests to wear green; its FAQ sets no other dress code. Free mobility scooters are offered first come, first served, Tuesday through Sunday, on Bell Road near the main entrance, and there are ADA viewing platforms at the 16th green, the 17th fairway and the 18th green. Tell the reservations team about mobility needs when you book, so the pickup and the unload point suit the rider. During the final 48 hours, verify addresses, contact numbers and the tournament’s newest parking and entry notes, and send one summary to riders. If staff change the approach on the day, the chauffeur follows them and the transportation lead relays the update. Reach the reservations team at (623) 986-6339 or reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com.

How is Phoenix Open transportation priced per person?

For 14 Phoenix Open riders sharing the Executive Black Sprinter for 6 billed hours, the published $145-per-hour rate comes to about $62 per person before tax for the whole shared ride; the price changes with the vehicle, the hours, the day and the confirmed plan. That example is arithmetic, not a flat tournament fare: the hourly rate times the billed hours, divided by the riders. If only ten people ride, divide by ten. A day that waits through the round and dinner after needs more hours than a drop-off and a set pickup, so describe the real pattern and let the quote price it. The same arithmetic on the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) uses its own rate of $175 an hour and its 16 seats; on the Maybach Jet Sprinter, $295 an hour for 9. The ready-made packages on this page print the engine’s own total for their hours and extras, including any hour the rate ladder gives free. One person collects the shares and one person owns the manifest. Neither job belongs to the chauffeur, and neither should wait until the group is standing at the curb after the round.

Frequently asked questions

When is the WM Phoenix Open 2027?

Monday, February 8 to Sunday, February 14, 2027, at TPC Scottsdale. Monday and Tuesday are Ford Free Days with free general admission, and the four tournament rounds run Thursday, February 11 to Sunday, February 14.

Where is the Phoenix Open played?

On the Stadium Course at TPC Scottsdale, 17020 North Hayden Road, Scottsdale, AZ 85255. The entrances are the Main Entrance at Bell, the Hayden Entrance and the Fairmont Scottsdale Princess Golf Entrance.

What time do gates open at the Phoenix Open?

Entry opens at 7:00 a.m. at the Main and Princess entrances and at 7:15 a.m. at Hayden. Play begins at 7:30 a.m. on Thursday and Friday and 9:00 a.m. on Saturday and Sunday. The entry times are undated, so recheck them in January.

Is parking free at the Phoenix Open?

The 2027 parking plan and any price are announced closer to the date. In 2026, general parking used remote lots at WestWorld and at Salt River Fields, which had a free shuttle. With a chauffeured ride nobody in the group drives or parks.

Where do Uber and Lyft drop off at the Phoenix Open?

In 2026, rideshares, taxis and all stop-and-drop used Lot R, entered from Pima Road; the 2027 plan is announced closer to the date. For the Birds Nest, rideshare pickup and drop-off is on Hartford Drive, south of Princess.

Can a limo or party bus drop off at the Phoenix Open gate?

No official page gives a limo, party bus or charter a gate or drop-off privilege, and some lots are reserved for pass types, charter buses included. Our chauffeur unloads where traffic staff direct and follows any 2027 instruction the tournament publishes.

What does it cost to get into the Phoenix Open?

Monday, February 8 and Tuesday, February 9 are Ford Free Days: free admission, no ticket needed. Guests 15 and younger get in free. Other admission is sold through AXS; the official site says its link is coming soon, so 2027 prices are announced closer to the date.

Where is the Coors Light Birds Nest?

At 82nd Street and Bell Road, across from the main tournament entrance, Wednesday, February 10 to Saturday, February 13, 2027. It is 21 and over, headliners usually go on at about 8:30 p.m., and rideshares use Hartford Drive, south of Princess.

What happens at the 16th hole during Phoenix Open week?

The week opens with the Concert in the Coliseum on the 16th hole on Saturday, February 6, 2027: Imagine Dragons, with Counting Crows opening, for guests 21 and over, gates at 3:30 p.m. The WHOOP Shot at Glory is on the 16th at 3:30 p.m. on Wednesday, February 10.

What should I wear to the Phoenix Open?

The tournament’s FAQ sets no general dress code. Saturday, February 13 is Green Out Saturday: wear green, and a donation goes to its Working for Tomorrow fund. Keep bags small: opaque up to 6 by 6 by 6 inches, clear up to 12 by 6 by 12.
